JUST IN: The Philippines, through the Department of Foreign Affairs, urges Thailand and Cambodia to "extend due consideration and care to innocent civilians" as the border conflict between the two ASEAN states escalates with deadly clashes.

At least nine persons were killed in the latest exchange of fire between Thai and Cambodian forces in the disputed area of the border located in Thailand's Surin province on Thursday (July 24, 2025), according to Anadolu News Agency.

DFA: We are hopeful our two fellow ASEAN member states will resolve this issue in accordance with international law and the peaceful settlement of disputes.

The Philippines does not take any position on this dispute but underscores the importance of maintaining open lines of communication and ensuring the de-escalation of the situation.

We are continually monitoring the situation and we are ready to extend all possible assistance to Filipinos living in these two countries if necessary.  

To date, no Filipino nationals have been reported to be affected by this conflict. | Joyce Rocamora

Matatandaan na isinara ang dalawang outfalls kasama ang Faura outfall para padaanin ang tubig-ulan sa Sewage Treatment Plant (STP).

‘NOT AN IOTA OF IMPROVEMENT’

Pinuna ni Catholic Bishops' Conference of the Philippines (CBCP) president Cardinal Pablo Virgilio David ang tila walang usad na proyekto ng gobyerno patungkol sa flood control, partikular na sa Malabon at Navotas.

Ayon kay David, hindi makitaan ng pag-unlad ang flood control projects ng pamahalaan kahit pa bilyon-bilyong piso ang inilaan para rito.

“Substandard flood control projects are a total waste of money. Obviously, flood control in our country has to be preceded by corruption control,” aniya.

Matatandaang ilang mga simbahan ang nalubog sa baha bunsod ng pag-ulang sanhi ng mga bagyo at Habagat.
